## Conclusion: False

There is no credible scientific evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19. The World Health Organization specifically states that there was no evidence that eating garlic protected people from infection with the novel coronavirus; there is likewise no basis to infer that boiling garlic in water makes it a COVID-19 cure. Garlic can be part of a normal diet, but it should not replace medical evaluation or evidence-based treatment.

The claim has circulated since early in the pandemic and has been repeatedly fact-checked. AFP reports that health professionals found no evidence for boiled garlic as an effective COVID-19 treatment. FDA also warns that products claiming to prevent, treat, or cure COVID-19 without evidence may be unsafe and have not been evaluated for effectiveness.

If someone has COVID-19—particularly if older, immunocompromised, pregnant, or living with chronic conditions—they should contact a clinician promptly to discuss appropriate care. Seek urgent/emergency help for trouble breathing, persistent chest pain or pressure, new confusion, inability to stay awake, or pale/blue/gray lips or skin.
